title: SELF DRIVE Act of 2026
summary: The bill would require automated-driving-system manufacturers to prepare evidence-backed safety cases for each system version, with a federal rule due by September 2027. It would also create a national crash data repository, requiring qualifying crash reports within 30 days or 10 days after notice and quarterly reports of automated-driving miles.

title: AV Safety Data Act
summary: The bill would require covered automated-driving and Level 2 driver-assistance manufacturers and operators to submit monthly vehicle-mileage, injury-crash, and unplanned-stoppage reports, alongside existing crash reporting. NHTSA would publish machine-readable data beginning 120 days after enactment, with rulemaking required within 90 days.

title: AV Emergency Response Coordination Act
summary: The bill would require autonomous-vehicle operators and manufacturers to provide standardized emergency-response guides and rescue sheets, maintain a 24-hour responder hotline answering within 30 seconds, and comply with government geofence notices within two minutes. It would direct NHTSA to establish national responder-coordination standards.

title: Autonomous Vehicle Acceleration Act of 2025
summary: The bill would direct the Transportation Secretary to address federal vehicle standards designed around human drivers within one year, including exemptions and reinterpretations for Level 4 and 5 vehicle designs. It would also require a national commercial-deployment roadmap, supplemental technology assessment, and congressional progress reports.

title: AMERICA DRIVES Act
summary: The bill would authorize Level 4 and 5 commercial vehicles to operate in interstate commerce without onboard or remote human drivers, overriding state human-occupant requirements. It would direct federal regulators by September 2027 to revise driver-centered trucking rules and exclude automated-driving equipment from vehicle-width measurements.

title: Shared Autonomous Mobility Act of 2026
summary: The bill would create a competitive federal grant program to deploy autonomous shared-mobility buses, allowing spending on vehicles and driving software. It proposes $60 million for fiscal 2027 and $40 million for 2028, reserves at least 15% for rural projects, and requires a dedicated autonomous-bus testing facility.
